Hi! I'm not a programmer, but I'd love a little tool for keeping track of shared costs when I go on trips with friends, so at the end we know who owes whom. Could you make it for me here?

My friend Sam writes scripts and is going to help me hook it up to a spreadsheet, so he wrote down how it should work. He says it should run with the Python that's already on my Mac, without installing anything else, by typing `python3 -m kitty` and a command in this folder, and it should keep everything in a file called `kitty.json` in the folder I run it from.

Here are the commands Sam wrote down:

- `init EUR` starts a new kitty, with EUR (or whatever we're using) as the main currency.
- `member add NAME`, `member remove NAME`, and `member list` for who's in the group.
- `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION` for when someone pays for something. By default it's split equally between everyone, and it should print the expense's ID number. Extras: `--among A,B` to split it equally between only some people; `--exact A=30,B=20`, `--shares A=2,B=1`, or `--percent A=60,B=40` to split it unevenly; `--currency USD` if it was paid in another currency; `--date 2026-07-14` (otherwise it's today); and `--category food` (otherwise "other").
- `expense list` and `expense remove ID`.
- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT` for when someone pays someone else back, also with `--currency` and `--date`.
- `rate set USD 0.92` means one USD is worth 0.92 of the main currency.
- `balances` shows how far up or down each person is overall: positive if they're owed money, negative if they owe.
- `settle` suggests who should pay whom to even everything out.
- `history NAME` lists everything that affected one person, with their running total.
- `report` shows how much each person spent on each category, counting their share of each expense, not what they paid.
- `export FILE` saves the expenses to a CSV file (for the spreadsheet) with the columns id, date, payer, description, amount, currency, category, and base_amount.

Sam also said the reports should print in a format called JSON so his scripts can read them, with money written as text with two decimals, in the main currency unless it's an expense's own amount. His examples:

- `member list`: `["Alice", "Bob"]`
- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

And if I type something wrong, like a name that isn't in the group or an amount that isn't a number, it should tell me what's wrong and stop (Sam says with "exit status 1"), not crash.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

"""Command-line interface and logic for the kitty tool.

All data lives in ./kitty.json. Money is handled with Decimal and stored as
strings with two decimals, so there are no floating-point rounding surprises.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")
CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem with the user's input or data; reported without a traceback."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_money(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    value = parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError("%s must be greater than zero, got %r" % (what, text))
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError("%s can have at most two decimals, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError("currency must be a three-letter code like EUR, got %r" % text)
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("date must look like 2026-07-14, got %r" % text)


def parse_pairs(text, option):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (name, value-text)."""
    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        item = item.strip()
        if not item:
            continue
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError("%s entries must look like NAME=VALUE, got %r" % (option, item))
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    if not pairs:
        raise KittyError("%s needs at least one NAME=VALUE entry" % option)
    return pairs


def fmt(value):
    return str(Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def today():
    return datetime.date.today().isoformat()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def data_path():
    return os.path.join(os.getcwd(), DATA_FILE)


def load():
    path = data_path()
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError("no %s in this folder; start one with: python3 -m kitty init EUR" % DATA_FILE)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError("could not read %s: %s" % (DATA_FILE, e))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "currency" not in data:
        raise KittyError("%s does not look like a kitty file" % DATA_FILE)
    return data


def save(data):
    # Write to a temporary file first, then swap it in, so a crash or a full
    # disk can never leave a half-written kitty.json behind.
    path = data_path()
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=os.path.dirname(path))
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.unlink(tmp)
        raise


def next_seq(data):
    # A running counter so entries on the same date keep the order they were added.
    data["seq"] = data.get("seq", 0) + 1
    return data["seq"]


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError("%r is not in the group (members: %s)"
                         % (name, ", ".join(data["members"]) or "none yet"))
    return name


def to_base(data, amount, currency):
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return amount
    rate = data["rates"].get(currency)
    if rate is None:
        raise KittyError("no exchange rate for %s yet; set one with: python3 -m kitty rate set %s 0.92"
                         % (currency, currency))
    return (amount * Decimal(rate)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` (a Decimal with cents) in proportion to `weights`.

    `weights` is an ordered list of (name, Decimal). Every cent is handed out:
    each person gets their rounded-down portion, then leftover cents go to
    whoever lost the most to rounding (earlier names first on ties). The
    resulting shares always add up exactly to `total`.
    """
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    cents = int((total / CENT).to_integral_value())
    portions = []
    for index, (name, weight) in enumerate(weights):
        exact = Decimal(cents) * weight / weight_sum
        floor = int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
        portions.append([name, floor, exact - floor, index])
    leftover = cents - sum(p[1] for p in portions)
    for p in sorted(portions, key=lambda p: (-p[2], p[3]))[:leftover]:
        p[1] += 1
    return {name: fmt(Decimal(c) * CENT) for name, c, _, _ in portions}


def split_weights(data, args, amount):
    """Turn the split options into an ordered list of (name, weight)."""
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent") if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")

    def check_names(names, option):
        seen = set()
        for name in names:
            require_member(data, name)
            if name in seen:
                raise KittyError("%s lists %r twice" % (option, name))
            seen.add(name)

    if args.among is not None:
        names = [n.strip() for n in args.among.split(",") if n.strip()]
        if not names:
            raise KittyError("--among needs at least one name")
        check_names(names, "--among")
        return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in names]

    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.exact, "--exact")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--exact")
        weights = [(n, parse_money(v, "--exact amount for %s" % n, allow_zero=True)) for n, v in pairs]
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError("--exact amounts add up to %s but the expense is %s" % (fmt(total), fmt(amount)))
        return weights

    if args.shares is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.shares, "--shares")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--shares")
        weights = []
        for n, v in pairs:
            w = parse_decimal(v, "--shares value for %s" % n)
            if w < 0:
                raise KittyError("--shares value for %s cannot be negative" % n)
            weights.append((n, w))
        if sum(w for _, w in weights) == 0:
            raise KittyError("--shares must add up to more than zero")
        return weights

    if args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.percent, "--percent")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--percent")
        weights = []
        for n, v in pairs:
            w = parse_decimal(v, "--percent value for %s" % n)
            if w < 0:
                raise KittyError("--percent value for %s cannot be negative" % n)
            weights.append((n, w))
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError("--percent values add up to %s, not 100" % total.normalize())
        return weights

    if not data["members"]:
        raise KittyError("the group has no members yet; add some with: python3 -m kitty member add NAME")
    return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in data["members"]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments as (date, seq, {person: change}, description), in order."""
    out = []
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        changes = {}
        changes[e["payer"]] = Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            changes[name] = changes.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
        out.append((e["date"], e["seq"], changes, e["description"]))
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        changes = {p["from"]: amount, p["to"]: -amount}
        out.append((p["date"], p["seq"], changes, "Payment from %s to %s" % (p["from"], p["to"])))
    out.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[0], ev[1]))
    return out


def compute_balances(data):
    balances = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["members"]}
    for _, _, changes, _ in events(data):
        for name, change in changes.items():
            balances[name] = balances.get(name, Decimal(0)) + change
    return balances


def compute_settlement(balances):
    """Greedy: the biggest debtor pays the biggest creditor until everyone is even."""
    debtors = [[name, -b] for name, b in balances.items() if b < 0]
    creditors = [[name, b] for name, b in balances.items() if b > 0]
    transfers = []
    while debtors and creditors:
        debtors.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        creditors.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        debtor, creditor = debtors[0], creditors[0]
        amount = min(debtor[1], creditor[1])
        transfers.append({"from": debtor[0], "to": creditor[0], "amount": fmt(amount)})
        debtor[1] -= amount
        creditor[1] -= amount
        if debtor[1] == 0:
            debtors.pop(0)
        if creditor[1] == 0:
            creditors.pop(0)
    return transfers


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def emit(obj):
    print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False))


def cmd_init(args):
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)

All data lives in ./kitty.json. Money is handled with Decimal and stored as
strings with two decimals, so there are no floating-point rounding surprises.

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")
CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem with the user's input or data; reported without a traceback."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_money(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    value = parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError("%s must be greater than zero, got %r" % (what, text))
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError("%s can have at most two decimals, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError("currency must be a three-letter code like EUR, got %r" % text)
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("date must look like 2026-07-14, got %r" % text)


def parse_pairs(text, option):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (name, value-text)."""
    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        item = item.strip()
        if not item:
            continue
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError("%s entries must look like NAME=VALUE, got %r" % (option, item))
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    if not pairs:
        raise KittyError("%s needs at least one NAME=VALUE entry" % option)
    return pairs


def fmt(value):
    return str(Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def today():
    return datetime.date.today().isoformat()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def data_path():
    return os.path.join(os.getcwd(), DATA_FILE)


def load():
    path = data_path()
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError("no %s in this folder; start one with: python3 -m kitty init EUR" % DATA_FILE)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError("could not read %s: %s" % (DATA_FILE, e))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "currency" not in data:
        raise KittyError("%s does not look like a kitty file" % DATA_FILE)
    return data


def save(data):
    # Write to a temporary file first, then swap it in, so a crash or a full
    # disk can never leave a half-written kitty.json behind.
    path = data_path()
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=os.path.dirname(path))
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")

    except BaseException:

def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` (a Decimal with cents) in proportion to `weights`.

    `weights` is an ordered list of (name, Decimal). Every cent is handed out:
    each person gets their rounded-down portion, then leftover cents go to
    whoever lost the most to rounding (earlier names first on ties). The
    resulting shares always add up exactly to `total`.
    """
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    cents = int((total / CENT).to_integral_value())
    portions = []
    for index, (name, weight) in enumerate(weights):
        exact = Decimal(cents) * weight / weight_sum
        floor = int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
        portions.append([name, floor, exact - floor, index])
    leftover = cents - sum(p[1] for p in portions)
    for p in sorted(portions, key=lambda p: (-p[2], p[3]))[:leftover]:
        p[1] += 1
    return {name: fmt(Decimal(c) * CENT) for name, c, _, _ in portions}

    """Turn the split options into an ordered list of (name, weight)."""
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent") if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")

            require_member(data, name)

            raise KittyError("--shares must add up to more than zero")
        return weights

            w = parse_decimal(v, "--percent value for %s" % n)

        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError("--percent values add up to %s, not 100" % total.normalize())
        return weights

        raise KittyError("the group has no members yet; add some with: python3 -m kitty member add NAME")
    return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in data["members"]]

def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments as (date, seq, {person: change}, description), in order."""

    balances = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["members"]}

def compute_settlement(balances):
    """Greedy: the biggest debtor pays the biggest creditor until everyone is even."""
    debtors = [[name, -b] for name, b in balances.items() if b < 0]
    creditors = [[name, b] for name, b in balances.items() if b > 0]
    transfers = []
    while debtors and creditors:

        debtor, creditor = debtors[0], creditors[0]

        creditor[1] -= amount
        if debtor[1] == 0:

        if creditor[1] == 0:

    return transfers

"""Command-line interface and logic for the kitty tool.

All data lives in ./kitty.json. Money is handled with Decimal and stored as
strings with two decimals, so there are no floating-point rounding surprises.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

DATA_FILE = "kitty.json"
CENT = Decimal("0.01")
CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{3}$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A problem with the user's input or data; reported without a traceback."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError("%s must be a number, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_money(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    value = parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError("%s must be greater than zero, got %r" % (what, text))
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError("%s can have at most two decimals, got %r" % (what, text))
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if not CURRENCY_RE.match(code):
        raise KittyError("currency must be a three-letter code like EUR, got %r" % text)
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("date must look like 2026-07-14, got %r" % text)


def parse_pairs(text, option):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (name, value-text)."""
    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        item = item.strip()
        if not item:
            continue
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError("%s entries must look like NAME=VALUE, got %r" % (option, item))
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        pairs.append((name.strip(), value.strip()))
    if not pairs:
        raise KittyError("%s needs at least one NAME=VALUE entry" % option)
    return pairs


def fmt(value):
    return str(Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def today():
    return datetime.date.today().isoformat()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def data_path():
    return os.path.join(os.getcwd(), DATA_FILE)


def load():
    path = data_path()
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError("no %s in this folder; start one with: python3 -m kitty init EUR" % DATA_FILE)
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError("could not read %s: %s" % (DATA_FILE, e))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "currency" not in data:
        raise KittyError("%s does not look like a kitty file" % DATA_FILE)
    return data


def save(data):
    # Write to a temporary file first, then swap it in, so a crash or a full
    # disk can never leave a half-written kitty.json behind.
    path = data_path()
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=os.path.dirname(path))
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.unlink(tmp)
        raise


def next_seq(data):
    # A running counter so entries on the same date keep the order they were added.
    data["seq"] = data.get("seq", 0) + 1
    return data["seq"]


def require_member(data, name):
    if name not in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError("%r is not in the group (members: %s)"
                         % (name, ", ".join(data["members"]) or "none yet"))
    return name


def to_base(data, amount, currency):
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return amount
    rate = data["rates"].get(currency)
    if rate is None:
        raise KittyError("no exchange rate for %s yet; set one with: python3 -m kitty rate set %s 0.92"
                         % (currency, currency))
    return (amount * Decimal(rate)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Splitting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` (a Decimal with cents) in proportion to `weights`.

    `weights` is an ordered list of (name, Decimal). Every cent is handed out:
    each person gets their rounded-down portion, then leftover cents go to
    whoever lost the most to rounding (earlier names first on ties). The
    resulting shares always add up exactly to `total`.
    """
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    cents = int((total / CENT).to_integral_value())
    portions = []
    for index, (name, weight) in enumerate(weights):
        exact = Decimal(cents) * weight / weight_sum
        floor = int(exact.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
        portions.append([name, floor, exact - floor, index])
    leftover = cents - sum(p[1] for p in portions)
    for p in sorted(portions, key=lambda p: (-p[2], p[3]))[:leftover]:
        p[1] += 1
    return {name: fmt(Decimal(c) * CENT) for name, c, _, _ in portions}


def split_weights(data, args, amount):
    """Turn the split options into an ordered list of (name, weight)."""
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent") if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")

    def check_names(names, option):
        seen = set()
        for name in names:
            require_member(data, name)
            if name in seen:
                raise KittyError("%s lists %r twice" % (option, name))
            seen.add(name)

    if args.among is not None:
        names = [n.strip() for n in args.among.split(",") if n.strip()]
        if not names:
            raise KittyError("--among needs at least one name")
        check_names(names, "--among")
        return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in names]

    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.exact, "--exact")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--exact")
        weights = [(n, parse_money(v, "--exact amount for %s" % n, allow_zero=True)) for n, v in pairs]
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError("--exact amounts add up to %s but the expense is %s" % (fmt(total), fmt(amount)))
        return weights

    if args.shares is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.shares, "--shares")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--shares")
        weights = []
        for n, v in pairs:
            w = parse_decimal(v, "--shares value for %s" % n)
            if w < 0:
                raise KittyError("--shares value for %s cannot be negative" % n)
            weights.append((n, w))
        if sum(w for _, w in weights) == 0:
            raise KittyError("--shares must add up to more than zero")
        return weights

    if args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(args.percent, "--percent")
        check_names([n for n, _ in pairs], "--percent")
        weights = []
        for n, v in pairs:
            w = parse_decimal(v, "--percent value for %s" % n)
            if w < 0:
                raise KittyError("--percent value for %s cannot be negative" % n)
            weights.append((n, w))
        total = sum(w for _, w in weights)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError("--percent values add up to %s, not 100" % total.normalize())
        return weights

    if not data["members"]:
        raise KittyError("the group has no members yet; add some with: python3 -m kitty member add NAME")
    return [(n, Decimal(1)) for n in data["members"]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments as (date, seq, {person: change}, description), in order."""
    out = []
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        changes = {}
        changes[e["payer"]] = Decimal(e["base_amount"])
        for name, share in e["shares"].items():
            changes[name] = changes.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
        out.append((e["date"], e["seq"], changes, e["description"]))
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = Decimal(p["base_amount"])
        changes = {p["from"]: amount, p["to"]: -amount}
        out.append((p["date"], p["seq"], changes, "Payment from %s to %s" % (p["from"], p["to"])))
    out.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[0], ev[1]))
    return out


def compute_balances(data):
    balances = {name: Decimal(0) for name in data["members"]}
    for _, _, changes, _ in events(data):
        for name, change in changes.items():
            balances[name] = balances.get(name, Decimal(0)) + change
    return balances


def compute_settlement(balances):
    """Greedy: the biggest debtor pays the biggest creditor until everyone is even."""
    debtors = [[name, -b] for name, b in balances.items() if b < 0]
    creditors = [[name, b] for name, b in balances.items() if b > 0]
    transfers = []
    while debtors and creditors:
        debtors.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        creditors.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        debtor, creditor = debtors[0], creditors[0]
        amount = min(debtor[1], creditor[1])
        transfers.append({"from": debtor[0], "to": creditor[0], "amount": fmt(amount)})
        debtor[1] -= amount
        creditor[1] -= amount
        if debtor[1] == 0:
            debtors.pop(0)
        if creditor[1] == 0:
            creditors.pop(0)
    return transfers

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False))

    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)

from contextlib import redirect_stderr, redirect_stdout
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty.cli import main

PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class KittyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.old_cwd = os.getcwd()
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        os.chdir(self.tmp.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        os.chdir(self.old_cwd)
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_cmd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(err):
            try:
                code = main(list(argv))
            except SystemExit as e:
                code = e.code
        return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def ok(self, *argv):
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        return out

    def js(self, *argv):
        return json.loads(self.ok(*argv))

    def fails(self, *argv):
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(code, 1, out)
        self.assertIn("error:", err)
        return err

    def group(self, *names):
        self.ok("init", "EUR")
        for n in names:
            self.ok("member", "add", n)

    # --- Sam's examples -----------------------------------------------------

    def test_sams_examples(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("member", "list"), ["Alice", "Bob"])
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                                 "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food").strip(), "1")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("expense", "list"), [{
            "id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
            "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
            "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("settle"), [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("history", "Bob"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("report"), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})

    def test_runs_as_module(self):
        self.group("Alice")
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=PROJECT)
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", "member", "list"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout), ["Alice"])
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", "balances", "extra"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)

    # --- splitting ----------------------------------------------------------

    def shares_of(self, expense_id=1):
        return {e["id"]: e for e in self.js("expense", "list")}[expense_id]["shares"]

    def test_default_split_and_leftover_cents(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "Taxi")
        shares = self.shares_of()
        self.assertEqual(shares, {"A": "3.34", "B": "3.33", "C": "3.33"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"A": "6.66", "B": "-3.33", "C": "-3.33"})

    def test_among(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "C", "30", "Wine", "--among", "A,B")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(), {"A": "15.00", "B": "15.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"A": "-15.00", "B": "-15.00", "C": "30.00"})

    def test_exact_shares_percent(self):
        self.group("A", "B")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "50", "x", "--exact", "A=30,B=20")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"A": "30.00", "B": "20.00"})
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "x", "--shares", "A=2,B=1")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(2), {"A": "6.67", "B": "3.33"})
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "x", "--percent", "A=60,B=40")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(3), {"A": "6.00", "B": "4.00"})

    def test_exact_in_foreign_currency_converts(self):
        self.group("A", "B")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "50", "x", "--currency", "usd", "--exact", "A=30,B=20")
        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "USD")
        self.assertEqual(e["base_amount"], "46.00")
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], {"A": "27.60", "B": "18.40"})

    def test_shares_always_sum_to_total(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "GBP", "1.1713")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "99.99", "x", "--currency", "GBP", "--shares", "A=1,B=1,C=1")
        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]
        self.assertEqual(sum(Decimal(v) for v in e["shares"].values()), Decimal(e["base_amount"]))

    def test_multiword_description_and_defaults(self):
        self.group("A", "B")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "12.5", "Beach", "umbrella", "rental", "--category", "fun")
        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]

    def test_ids_are_not_reused(self):

        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "1", "x")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "2", "y")
        self.ok("expense", "remove", "2")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "3", "z").strip(), "3")
        self.assertEqual([e["id"] for e in self.js("expense", "list")], [1, 3])

    def test_payment_evens_out(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "40", "Dinner")
        self.ok("payment", "add", "Bob", "Alice", "20")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"Alice": "0.00", "Bob": "0.00"})

        self.group("A", "B", "C", "D")

        self.ok("expense", "add", "B", "20", "Snacks")

        self.assertEqual(balances, {"A": "70.00", "B": "-10.00", "C": "-30.00", "D": "-30.00"})

import csv
import io
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr, redirect_stdout
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty.cli import main

PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class KittyTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.old_cwd = os.getcwd()
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        os.chdir(self.tmp.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        os.chdir(self.old_cwd)
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_cmd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(err):
            try:
                code = main(list(argv))
            except SystemExit as e:
                code = e.code
        return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def ok(self, *argv):
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        return out

    def js(self, *argv):
        return json.loads(self.ok(*argv))

    def fails(self, *argv):
        code, out, err = self.run_cmd(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(code, 1, out)
        self.assertIn("error:", err)
        return err

    def group(self, *names):
        self.ok("init", "EUR")
        for n in names:
            self.ok("member", "add", n)

    # --- Sam's examples -----------------------------------------------------

    def test_sams_examples(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("member", "list"), ["Alice", "Bob"])
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner", "--currency", "USD",
                                 "--date", "2026-07-14", "--category", "food").strip(), "1")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("expense", "list"), [{
            "id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner",
            "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
            "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("settle"), [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("history", "Bob"), [
            {"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}])
        self.assertEqual(self.js("report"), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})

    def test_runs_as_module(self):
        self.group("Alice")
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=PROJECT)
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", "member", "list"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout), ["Alice"])
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty", "balances", "extra"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)

    # --- splitting ----------------------------------------------------------

    def shares_of(self, expense_id=1):
        return {e["id"]: e for e in self.js("expense", "list")}[expense_id]["shares"]

    def test_default_split_and_leftover_cents(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "Taxi")
        shares = self.shares_of()
        self.assertEqual(shares, {"A": "3.34", "B": "3.33", "C": "3.33"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"A": "6.66", "B": "-3.33", "C": "-3.33"})

    def test_among(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "C", "30", "Wine", "--among", "A,B")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(), {"A": "15.00", "B": "15.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"A": "-15.00", "B": "-15.00", "C": "30.00"})

    def test_exact_shares_percent(self):
        self.group("A", "B")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "50", "x", "--exact", "A=30,B=20")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"A": "30.00", "B": "20.00"})
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "x", "--shares", "A=2,B=1")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(2), {"A": "6.67", "B": "3.33"})
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "10", "x", "--percent", "A=60,B=40")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(3), {"A": "6.00", "B": "4.00"})

    def test_exact_in_foreign_currency_converts(self):

        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "50", "x", "--currency", "usd", "--exact", "A=30,B=20")
        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]

        self.assertEqual(e["base_amount"], "46.00")
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], {"A": "27.60", "B": "18.40"})

    def test_shares_always_sum_to_total(self):

        self.ok("rate", "set", "GBP", "1.1713")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "99.99", "x", "--currency", "GBP", "--shares", "A=1,B=1,C=1")
        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]
        self.assertEqual(sum(Decimal(v) for v in e["shares"].values()), Decimal(e["base_amount"]))

    def test_multiword_description_and_defaults(self):

        e = self.js("expense", "list")[0]

        self.assertRegex(e["date"], r"^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d$")

    def test_ids_are_not_reused(self):

        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "1", "x")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "2", "y")
        self.ok("expense", "remove", "2")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "3", "z").strip(), "3")
        self.assertEqual([e["id"] for e in self.js("expense", "list")], [1, 3])

    # --- payments, settle, history -------------------------------------------

    def test_payment_evens_out(self):
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "40", "Dinner")
        self.ok("payment", "add", "Bob", "Alice", "20")
        self.assertEqual(self.js("balances"), {"Alice": "0.00", "Bob": "0.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.js("settle"), [])

    def test_settle_many_people(self):
        self.group("A", "B", "C", "D")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "A", "100", "Hotel")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "B", "20", "Snacks")
        balances = self.js("balances")
        self.assertEqual(balances, {"A": "70.00", "B": "-10.00", "C": "-30.00", "D": "-30.00"})
        totals = {k: Decimal(v) for k, v in balances.items()}
